sn12.58:1.2: “Bhikkhus, when one dwells contemplating gratification in things that can fetter, there is a descent of name-and-form.
sn12.58:1.3: With name-and-form as condition, the six sense bases [come to be]….
sn12.58:1.4: Such is the origin of this whole mass of suffering.
sn12.58:2.1: “Suppose, bhikkhus, there was a great tree, and all its roots going downwards and across would send the sap upwards.
sn12.58:2.3: Sustained by that sap, nourished by it, that great tree would stand for a very long time.
sn12.58:2.4: So too, when one lives contemplating gratification in things that can fetter, there is a descent of name-and-form…. Such is the origin of this whole mass of suffering.
sn12.58:3.1: “When, bhikkhus, one dwells contemplating danger in things that can fetter, there is no descent of name-and-form.
sn12.58:3.2: With the cessation of name-and-form comes cessation of the six sense bases….
sn12.58:3.3: Such is the cessation of this whole mass of suffering.
sn12.58:4.1: “Suppose, bhikkhus, there was a great tree.
sn12.58:4.2: Then a man would come along bringing a shovel and a basket. He would cut down the tree at its foot … he would winnow the ashes in a strong wind or let them be carried away by the swift current of a river.
sn12.58:4.3: Thus that great tree would be cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, obliterated so that it is no more subject to future arising.
sn12.58:4.4: “So too, bhikkhus, when one dwells contemplating danger in things that can fetter, there is no descent of name-and-form….
sn12.58:4.6: Such is the cessation of this whole mass of suffering.”
